name: Greece
tagline: Public universities teach in Greek; the English routes are few and paid
summary: Greek public universities are free and highly regarded, but they teach in Greek, and entry for Greek-speaking students runs through the national Panhellenic examinations. Since a 2022 law change, a small number of public universities have been allowed to run separate English-taught undergraduate programmes with tuition fees, and these are the realistic route for a Danish IB student. There are only a handful of them, they are genuinely good, and they cost between EUR 6,000 and EUR 17,000 a year. Beyond that there is the private, American-accredited college sector.
whyConsider: The University of Athens runs a 6-year MD taught entirely in English with clinical training across sixteen Athens hospitals
Its BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece is taught in English for EUR 6,000 a year - studying ancient Greece in Athens
Living costs are low by Northern European standards and you are an EU citizen, so no visa
English-taught programmes accept the IB directly rather than requiring the Panhellenic examinations
The American College of Greece teaches in English with US accreditation if you want a liberal-arts style degree
watchOuts: The overwhelming majority of Greek bachelor teaching is in Greek - do not assume a department has an English track
English-taught programmes at public universities charge tuition, unlike the Greek-taught ones
The English-taught MD at Athens costs EUR 17,000 a year for six years and requires UCAT or MCAT on top of your IB
The Athens MD’s own admission page contradicts itself about whether a current-year IB candidate may apply at all - get an answer in writing from medicen@uoa.gr before you plan around it
Deadlines are set programme by programme, and some English-taught programmes publish no deadline anywhere
The Ministry route for Greek-taught public places opens for about eight days in early July, exactly when IB results land, and the system locks the moment it closes

Several basic facts - how the foreign-nationals quota is scored, work rights, student housing and whether Greek-taught public study is free for EU citizens - could not be verified from official sources and need checking

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: Set per programme. The University of Athens MD in English requires at least 36 points overall. Its BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece asks for an 'indicative average grade' of 70% or equivalent.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University of Athens MD in English requires 36 points overall 'including three higher-level subjects (two of them should be selected from Physics, Chemistry, and Biology)'.
notes: The English-taught programmes accept the IB Diploma directly as a school-leaving qualification - you do not sit the Panhellenic examinations for them.

Admission to Greek-taught public programmes is controlled by the Ministry of Education. A graduate of a school in an EU member state, with at least one parent not of Greek descent, applies through the ministry's foreign-nationals special category (sub-category B1) in its eight-day July window, and must show a B2 Greek certificate to enrol. Source: ministry circular Φ.152/117735/Α5 of 9 September 2026, read 2026-09-23.
Whether DOATAP or another recognition step is required for an IB Diploma was not confirmed on the pages read.

portal.name: Study in Greece (@SiG application platform) and the Ministry's programme finder

deadlines.label: Ministry of Education application window for foreign nationals - eight days in July
deadlines.audience: applicants of non-Greek descent, for Greek-taught public places
deadlines.notes: Greece does have a national route for a foreign qualification and it was missing from this profile entirely. It is the "αλλοδαποί - αλλογενείς" special category, run by the Ministry of Education on its own platform at https://exams-foreigner.it.minedu.gov.gr, and it is how a non-Greek applicant with a foreign school-leaving qualification competes for a place on a Greek-taught public programme without sitting the Panhellenic examinations. The window is eight days long. For the 2026-2027 year the Ministry announced, in Greek, that candidates were "καλούνται να υποβάλουν ηλεκτρονικά (μέσω διαδικτύου) αίτηση - μηχανογραφικό δελτίο" from "Πέμπτη 2 Ιουλίου μέχρι και την Πέμπτη 9 Ιουλίου 2026" - Thursday 2 July to Thursday 9 July 2026. There is no grace: "Μετά την παρέλευση της παραπάνω προθεσμίας υποβολής δεν θα γίνονται δεκτές εκπρόθεσμες αιτήσεις ... καθώς κλειδώνει το σύστημα" - after the deadline the system locks and late applications are not accepted. You must already hold every supporting document when you apply. You may not also apply in the "Έλληνες του Εξωτερικού" category in the same year, and false documents mean deletion plus exclusion from every Greek admission process for the following two academic years. The 2027-2028 announcement had not appeared on 23 September 2026, which is why no date is recorded; the Ministry publishes it about a day before the window opens, so watch https://www.minedu.gov.gr/allogeneis-m/anakoinwseis-allodapoi from late June 2027. Read in Greek. The eight days fall exactly when IB results are released, so assemble the documents in June rather than waiting.

deadlines.label: Ministry route - supporting documents by courier, the day after the form closes
deadlines.audience: applicants of non-Greek descent, for Greek-taught public places
deadlines.notes: Promoted to its own entry because it is a second deadline a day after the first, sent a different way, and missing it wastes the application. For the 2026-2027 year the Ministry set the courier postmark date as "Παρασκευή 10 Ιουλίου 2026" - Friday 10 July 2026, delivery accepted 10:00 to 14:00, and by courier only. What must go in the envelope is a printed copy of the submitted αίτηση - μηχανογραφικό δελτίο and a copy of the required Υπεύθυνη Δήλωση (sworn declaration). The full set of qualifying documents is handed in later, to the department you are admitted to, on the enrolment dates it sets. The 2027-2028 dates were not published on 23 September 2026. Read in Greek.

deadlines.label: University of Athens - BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece
deadlines.notes: The page year-stamps its own deadline, so it cannot honestly be rolled forward: "Application Deadlines for the academic year 2026-2027: 1 August for applicants required to issue a student visa (D1.1) / 1 August for applicants not required to issue a student visa (D1.1)". An earlier pass carried this as 1 August 2027; the university has published no 2027-2028 date, so it is recorded as not yet announced with 1 August 2026 as precedent. Read on 23 September 2026, when the page still displayed "Now Open" above a deadline that had passed seven weeks earlier and an academic year that had already begun - so the page is not maintained closely enough to plan against, and an email is worth more than a re-read. Two payment dates come after admission and are published only as months: tuition is 6,000 euros a year in two instalments, the first "due by the end of June" and the second "due by the end of January", with a deposit possibly required to secure the place. Entry is on an IB Diploma with an indicative average of 70 per cent, plus TOEFL 88 or IELTS 6.5.

deadlines.label: University of Athens MD in English - no deadline published, and the page disagrees with itself about whether you can apply at all
deadlines.notes: "Date not published" is our wording and it is the truth twice over: the programme publishes no application deadline on any of its three admissions pages, and the one page that describes eligibility contradicts itself about whether a candidate sitting the IB this year may apply. Clause A of the admission requirements says an eligible applicant "should have obtained a high school diploma (July 2025 or earlier) or equivalent secondary education diploma" - read literally, for that intake you needed a diploma from the summer before last, which would put a May 2027 IB candidate into the 2028 intake, not the 2027 one. The same page then says the opposite twice: the IB criterion is "Applicants must have achieved (or be predicted to achieve) at least 36 points overall", and the General Remarks say "All applicants who expect to obtain their baccalaureate or A-Levels results after the deadline of applications, must include official predicted scores issued by their school." Both readings are on the same page, which was last modified on 28 May 2026 and was read on 23 September 2026. We are not going to resolve it to the more convenient reading, because the convenient reading costs a year if it is wrong. What to do instead: write to medicen@uoa.gr, state that you complete the IB in May 2027 and ask in terms whether you may apply for entry in 2027 on predicted scores, and get the answer in writing before you build a plan around it. On timing, the only date the programme published for the 2026 cycle was a document cut-off buried in the same paragraph - a pre-med or bachelor’s transcript "no later than 30/04/2026" - which suggests the cycle closes in spring rather than in summer. Entry is 36 points including three higher-level subjects, two of them from Physics, Chemistry and Biology, plus UCAT or MCAT and IELTS 7.5 with 6.5 in each component.

deadlines.label: University of Athens MD - pay the 5,000 euro deposit or lose the place
deadlines.notes: A per-applicant deadline with no public date, which is exactly the kind that gets missed. The programme says: "An admission letter (conditional or unconditional) will be sent to you if you have successfully passed the interview. To secure a place in the program you will need to proceed with paying the amount of €5,000, within the deadline set in the admission letter." The deposit is non-refundable and is followed by two further instalments totalling 12,000 euros, in September and January. Nothing on the site says how long you get, so read the admission letter the day it arrives and diarise the date it gives you.

steps: Decide which route you are taking. For a Danish IB student there are three, and they are genuinely different: an English-taught programme at a public university, a Greek-taught public place through the Ministry’s foreign-nationals category, or a private English-language college such as ACG/Deree.

If you want a Greek-taught public place, the Ministry is your deadline, not the university. The αλλοδαποί-αλλογενείς window is about eight days in early July, on the Ministry’s own platform, and the system locks when it closes.

Find the programme. The Ministry of Education runs a programme finder at studies.minedu.gov.gr covering bachelor’s and master’s programmes in Greek and English, and Study in Greece runs the @SiG platform.
For an English-taught programme, apply directly to it. Each one runs its own application on its own timetable, and some publish no deadline at all — email the programme office rather than assuming.

Prepare English proof and, for medicine, an admissions test. The Athens MD accepts UCAT or MCAT and requires IELTS 7.5 overall with at least 6.5 in each component, TOEFL 80, or Cambridge FCE at B2. The Ancient Greece BA requires TOEFL 88 or IELTS 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each component.
Have every document ready before you apply, not after. The Ministry route requires you to hold the full set at the moment of submission, and false or missing papers carry a two-year exclusion.

Pay the deposit on acceptance, to the deadline in your own admission letter. The Athens MD takes a non-refundable EUR 5,000 deposit followed by two instalments of EUR 12,000 in total, in September and January.
As an EU citizen, move to Greece and register locally; there is no visa to apply for.
application.selectionNotes: The English-taught programmes select on your IB result, English proof and, for medicine, an admissions test, and each sets its own deadline - or none. Greek-taught public places are allocated through the Panhellenic examinations, with a separate special category for foreign nationals of non-Greek descent (αλλοδαποί-αλλογενείς) administered by the Ministry of Education on its own platform, with an eight-day application window in early July and a courier deadline the day after it closes. The mechanics of that category - which programmes carry a quota, how a foreign qualification is scored against it, and whether an IB Diploma needs any recognition step first - are not set out on the announcement that opens it, and could not be established from an official page on 23 September 2026. Check with the Ministry before relying on it.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Few. The Ministry's portal advertises 'over 200 study programs taught in English', but that count is dominated by master's programmes. At undergraduate level, the confirmed English-taught programmes at the University of Athens are the BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece, the MD programme in English, and the MPharm integrated master in Pharmacy. Aristotle University lists 41 undergraduate programmes but none were confirmed as English-taught. The International Hellenic University's undergraduate programmes are listed only in Greek; its 26 English-language programmes are all master's.
language.englishProof: Set per programme. University of Athens MD: TOEFL 80, IELTS 7.5 overall with at least 6.5 in each component, or Cambridge FCE at B2. BA in Ancient Greece: TOEFL 88 (with minimum 17 Listening, 17 Writing, 18 Reading, 20 Speaking), IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 5.5 in each component, or Cambridge FCE at B2. Native speakers are exempt. Whether IB English A or B is accepted in place of a test was not confirmed on the pages read.
notes: Greek is required for the vast majority of bachelor programmes at public universities. This is the single most important thing to understand about Greece.
The English-taught programmes are genuinely taught in English, including clinical teaching on the Athens MD.
You will need some Greek for everyday life outside the university, especially outside Athens.

tuitionEuEea.value: The English-taught programmes charge the same fee to EU and non-EU students. University of Athens MD in English: EUR 17,000 a year, with the page stating 'Tuition fees for the academic year 2026-2027 for EU and non-EU citizens are EUR 17.000'. University of Athens BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece: EUR 6,000 a year, paid in two instalments in June and January. Whether Greek-taught public bachelor study is free for EU citizens could not be verified from an official page read on 2026-09-22.
tuitionEuEea.year: 2026-2027 (MD); BAAG page undated but current on 2026-09-22

tuitionNonEu.value: Same as EU for the University of Athens English-taught programmes: EUR 17,000 a year for the MD, EUR 6,000 a year for the BA in Ancient Greece.

notes: The Athens MD requires a non-refundable EUR 5,000 deposit, then EUR 12,000 split across September and January.
Monthly living costs in Athens or Thessaloniki were not published on any official page read on 2026-09-22 and need checking before use.
Private college fees, including ACG/Deree, were not published on the pages read.

funding: No scholarship scheme aimed at EU bachelor applicants was verified from an official page. ACG/Deree advertises a merit scholarship for EU students but the amounts were not published on the pages read.
Danish SU for a full degree abroad requires programme approval by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen - check with your studievejleder.
Check each English-taught programme's own page; these are new programmes and scholarship arrangements change.
residency: As a Danish EU citizen you have the right to live and study in Greece and will normally register locally for stays over three months. Non-EU students need a student visa and residence permit. The specific Greek procedures, documents and timescales could not be verified from an official page on 2026-09-22 - the Study in Greece visa page directs non-EU students to a third-party visa service rather than setting out the rules.
healthcare: As an EU citizen bring your EU health insurance card for necessary care in the Greek public system. Detailed requirements for students, and what non-EU students must arrange, were not published on the pages read on 2026-09-22.

institutions.name: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
institutions.englishBachelors: Three confirmed: BA in Archaeology, History and Literature of Ancient Greece; MD programme in English; MPharm integrated master in Pharmacy
institutions.note: The oldest university in Greece and the only one with a real English-taught undergraduate offering - the MD at EUR 17,000 a year and the Ancient Greece BA at EUR 6,000.

institutions.name: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed. AUTh lists 41 undergraduate programmes but no English-taught bachelor was identified on the pages read.
institutions.note: The largest university in Greece and in the Balkans, but admission runs through the Ministry of Education and teaching is in Greek.

institutions.name: University of Crete
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: Research-strong, especially in physics and the life sciences through its links with FORTH, but bachelor teaching is in Greek.

institutions.name: National Technical University of Athens
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: Greece's leading engineering school, with five-year integrated diploma degrees - but taught in Greek.

institutions.name: Athens University of Economics and Business
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: The main economics and business university in Greece, with a strong research reputation in economics.

institutions.name: International Hellenic University
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Its undergraduate programmes are listed only in Greek; its 26 English-language programmes are master's.
institutions.note: The name promises more than the undergraduate reality - the English teaching here is at master's level, through its University Center for International Study Programs.

institutions.name: University of the Aegean
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: Spread across six Aegean islands, which is unusual and appealing, but teaching is in Greek.

institutions.name: University of Patras
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: A large research university in the Peloponnese, strongest in engineering and computer engineering.

institutions.name: University of Ioannina
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: In the mountains of Epirus, with a well-regarded medical school and a very low cost of living.

institutions.name: The American College of Greece (Deree)
institutions.englishBachelors: All undergraduate programmes are taught in English, awarding BA and BSc degrees across three schools
institutions.note: Private, American-accredited (NEASC) and entirely English-taught, with separate admission tracks for Greek, EU, North American and other applicants; tuition was not published on the pages read.

institutions.name: Athens School of Fine Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed; teaching is in Greek
institutions.note: Greece's national art school, with entry by portfolio and entrance examination, taught in Greek.

institutions.name: University of Piraeus
institutions.englishBachelors: None confirmed on the pages read
institutions.note: Known above all for maritime studies and shipping, which fits the port city it sits in.
